group_scores.rationale: This is the world benchmark (VWRA.L), so its score against the world is 0 by construction. The absolute backdrop was risk-off: the S&P 500 fell into correction, the VIX went above 30 (CNBC), the minutes are hawkish (T1) and a December hike is fully priced. In the local cache VT fell 8.5% from Nov 13 to Nov 20. This sets the logged risk label only.
group_scores.falsifier: Not applicable to the relative score, because this is the benchmark.

group_scores.rationale: The Fed headwinds are US-specific: the hawkish minutes, Cook and Jefferson (all T1), Waller's 50bp talk, and the AI valuation and financing risk flagged in the minutes. They are offset by global tightening: UK CPI 3.6%, euro-area HICP 4.0%, and Ueda and Takata pointing to more BoJ hikes. Cached SPY was -0.05pp against VT in the window. US data were mixed (claims 203k, retail +0.2%), so there is no 1-3 month edge.
group_scores.falsifier: A 50bp December hike or hawkish 2027 dots while non-US central banks pause would mean -1. A Fed signal of a pause after December, with an AI-led rebound, would mean +1.

group_scores.rationale: Headline inflation re-accelerated: UK CPI 3.6% (verified), euro-area HICP 4.0%, and Japan CPI 2.3%. Core inflation is contained (UK 2.8%, euro area 2.6%, Japan core-core 2.2%). Bailey and Ueda leaned hawkish, while Lagarde gave no guidance. The pack shows EFA -1.49pp in 1w, but the cached closes give +0.80pp against VT, so the lag is not confirmed.
group_scores.falsifier: BoE or ECB December hike repricing, or a JGB selloff, would mean -1. A BoJ hike with a sharp USDJPY fall and stable equities would mean +1.

group_scores.rationale: There was no China easing: the Nov 20 LPR was unchanged at 3.0%/3.5% and PBoC releases from Nov 14-20 show no RRR cut. The broad dollar is up 3.2% over 3m (MAC05), a headwind. Verifier counter-fact: the pack's EEM +3.75pp 1w is not reproduced by the cache, where EEM fell 11.6% (-3.1pp against VT, Nov 13-20). The 'unexplained outperformance' premise is likely a data artefact.
group_scores.falsifier: T2-confirmed China stimulus or PBoC easing, or a sustained dollar reversal, would mean +1. A larger US hike that pushes the dollar higher would mean -1.

group_scores.rationale: The policy path is hawkish across central banks. The FOMC minutes (T1, verified) show almost all participants favour further hikes, a couple are open to more than 25bp (the lead said 'some'), and staff flag a risk of unanchored expectations. Cook (T1, verified) and Jefferson back a stronger response, and CNBC (T2, verified) reports a December hike fully priced. UK and euro-area inflation rose, and the ECB FSR (verified) warns of a global repricing of sovereign risk. Strong counter-fact: in the window the 10y fell 23bp (verified) and cached IEF rose 1.79% while VT fell 8.5%. That is about +10pp against the world, a strong hedge in a risk-off week. It argues against confidence above low.
group_scores.falsifier: Softer November CPI or payrolls, a Fed signal of a pause after December, or a growth or AI-credit shock that keeps the 10y below about 4.8% and IEF ahead of the world would mean 0 or +1.

group_scores.rationale: The forces offset. The hawkish Fed path (T1) raises the real-rate cost, but 10y TIPS yields fell from 2.91% to 2.77% in the window (T1). No in-window source on central-bank buying was found. Cached GLD fell 9.2% in absolute terms but was only -0.65pp against VT.
group_scores.falsifier: 10y real yields above about 3% on a 50bp hike would mean -1. Real yields below about 2.5%, or a central-bank buying or geopolitical shock, would mean +1.
